google:Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25KaGIyU.author: Daria Samoylova
google:Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT25KaGIyU.text:
My first impression of this gym was excellent. I was ready to give it five stars and praise the scale of the facility, the equipment, and everything it has to offer.

Unfortunately, after three consecutive days of being approached by staff over issues that had nothing to do with me, my opinion changed completely.

Day 1. A staff member came to tell me not to bring drinks in shaker bottles into the gym. The problem is that I don’t even own a shaker bottle and had never brought one with me during the two weeks I’d been training there. When I asked why they were addressing this to me personally, I was told that some man had spilled coffee. I still don’t understand why I was the person being lectured about someone else’s behavior.

Day 2. I was stopped and given another lecture because I had taken a step platform from the yoga room. It was only my second week at the gym. I simply didn’t know there was another place to get them. I wasn’t breaking rules on purpose or trying to inconvenience anyone, yet I was treated as though I had done something wrong.

Day 3. I arrived wearing Crocs because the previous day I had seen another member training in Crocs. The written rules only stated that training barefoot or in flip-flops was prohibited. Nothing mentioned Crocs.

When staff told me I couldn’t train, I politely asked them to show me where this rule was written. They brought me the rules, which indeed mentioned only bare feet and flip-flops - not Crocs.

I wasn’t looking for an argument. I said, “No problem, I’ll check my car for sneakers.” I went to my car, couldn’t find them, came back, apologized, and explained that next time I would absolutely wear proper training shoes.

Despite that, I was refused entry to a gym.

For context, I’ve been training for over ten years. I wasn’t planning to deadlift or do Olympic lifting. I was going to do a shoulder workout. Nevertheless, I was left standing at reception until someone called a manager to get permission to let me in. And stayed just at the 1st floor, so I did not finish my full workout.

This wasn’t about safety anymore.
It was about customer service.

I have no problem following rules. If a gym changes its policies, just communicate them clearly. But repeatedly approaching the same customer three days in a row over unrelated issues - and finally refusing entry over a rule that wasn’t even written anywhere - is simply poor service.

I’ll finish my membership because I’ve already paid for it. But instead of feeling welcome, supported, and part of a fitness community, I ended up feeling constantly watched, corrected, and made to feel guilty.

That is not the atmosphere of a premium gym.

We came to Ludus Spa for a massage after a workout and it was exactly what we needed. 

The reception team Peach, Aom, Janis, and Bee were incredibly warm and welcoming. Posh also gave us great recommendations and made sure we had the best experience.

The therapists here are highly professional, and the natural products they use smell amazing and leave a long lasting scent on the skin. The treatment was definitely worth the price, every single Baht

One thing we really loved is that all rooms are private. My partner and I had a couples massage room, which felt very comfortable. We left feeling completely refreshed.

What makes Ludus even better is that it’s a complete wellness destination, with fitness facilities, a spa, and a restaurant all in one place.

We’ll definitely be coming back again!
